rationale: C03 is an especially strong drafting-template candidate: it concerns the identical carrier, uses the same three-part WHEREAS sequence, and repeats both operative provisions nearly verbatim. The later directive principally substitutes a different employee representative and a new date. C02 and C04 share essentially the same machinery and language, but C03's identical carrier and factual formulation make it the most plausible direct template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS a dispute exists between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines), a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas a dispute exists between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines), a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen
shared_material.explanation: The later order preserves the entire party-identification clause and changes only the represented employee organization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a large section of the country of essential transportation service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas this dispute, in the Judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a large section of the country of essential transportation service
shared_material.explanation: This factual predicate is effectively verbatim, including the distinctive description of harm to a large section of the country.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order. As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement shall be made by the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) or its employees in the conditions out of which the said dispute arose.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order. As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) or its employees in the conditions out of which the said dispute arose.
shared_material.explanation: The complete operative sequence—thirty-day reporting followed by a section 10 status-quo requirement applied to the same carrier—is reproduced nearly word for word.
